question.problem:
A continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function 

$$
f(x)=\frac{2}{{x}^{2}},\,1\le x\le 2.
$$

Calculate $\text{E}[{X}^{5}].$

current_example.problem:
A continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14133327/assets/460f3d49d0d07ec4c989c6c52dea6449f600a20271ae6e182fb13cee28fd8c13.svg)

Calculate $\textrm E [X^4].$
current_example.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ the $n$th raw moment of $X$ is given by

$$
\textrm{E}[X^n] = \int_{S} x^n \cdot f(x) \,\textrm{d}x.
$$

So, we compute the fourth raw moment of $X$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{4}] & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{4}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{4}\cdot (1-x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{2}{x}^{4}\cdot \frac{1}{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{4}-{x}^{5})\,\text{d}x+\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{1}^{2}{x}^{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(\frac{1}{5}\,{x}^{5}-\frac{1}{6}\,{x}^{6})\,{|}_{0}^{1}+\frac{1}{10}\,{x}^{5}\,{|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =(\frac{1}{5}-\frac{1}{6}-0)+\frac{1}{10}(32-1) \\  & =\frac{1}{30}+\frac{31}{10} \\  & =\frac{47}{15}\end{aligned}
$$
